parsed.basis: Split-Dalmatia combines Croatia's national framework — no criminalisation of same-sex conduct, hate-crime law covering gender identity, and anti-discrimination protections whose enforcement is inconsistent — with a strongly tourist-facing coastal economy centred on Split, a major port and cruise destination where foreign visitors are routine, an LGBTI centre has operated since the mid-2010s, and Pride events are held. Island and coastal towns have visible gay-friendly venues and beaches, while inland and smaller settlements are more socially conservative and public displays of affection can draw unwelcome attention, with limited local recourse beyond national institutions.
